newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee remains untraded on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee remains untraded on Friday.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which opened quoted close to the Central Bank's selling level on Friday, was untraded as banks refused to quote two-way prices, dealers said.
At 0545 GMT the rupee was quoted at its opening level of 59.18 to the dollar. The rupee closed at 59.20 on Thursday.

"Since the market rate is already near the Central Bank's selling level, we want to know whether they (Central Bank) will sell dollars to us if the exchange rate goes over the top," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by five local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.0289 and 59.2012.
The Central Bank sells dollars only for covering imports.
Overnight call money rates were volatile in early Friday trade before settling down at 8.75 percent, dealers said.
"Call rates opened at 8.5 percent and even rose to 12 percent before settling down," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Call money was volatile due to a slight tightness in money supply after banks covered imports with dollars from the Central Bank on Wednesday and Thursday, dealers said.
